input.title: Request about a transfer to the wrong recipient
input.request: I sent a £286.40 transfer for a shared pottery-studio bill to the wrong saved recipient. Please register a request to seek its return.

events.text: Transfer status: sent. This status confirms the transfer was sent from your H&V account; it does not confirm that the recipient has returned the money.

summary: The customer asked the desk to register a request to seek the return of a £286.40 transfer sent to the wrong saved recipient. The desk classified it as a registration request about a transfer, refused a separate "ask the payment system" step because the rules did not allow it for a registration, and registered the request with the payment team, where the case closed as submitted. Nothing in the record confirms which payment or recipient was involved beyond what the customer said, and whether the money comes back is not decided.

About this desk:
A bank's service desk (Harrow & Vale Bank, fictional). The bank never acts or approves for someone else, never handles a PIN or a password, and never claims more than a record shows.

The case stops at one moment: choose the bank's next step from here with one tool, then stop. The facts are what the desk read from the bank's records; a fact not listed is not known yet. I've submitted your request to seek the return of the £286.40 transfer to the wrong saved recipient. It's now with the team that handles these cases.

I couldn't look up the payment record first, because the desk wouldn't run that check for a registration request. So the request rests on the amount and details you gave, and I haven't confirmed which payment or recipient it is. I can't say yet whether the money will come back.
